summary.en: Daughter of a Lạc lord of Mê Linh who, with her sister Trưng Nhị, led the rising of 40 against Han rule and was proclaimed queen. Defeated by Ma Yuan in 43, the sisters are revered as national heroines in Vietnam.
summary.zh: 麊泠雒将之女，40年与妹妹征贰起兵反抗东汉统治并被拥立为王。43年被马援击败，姐妹二人在越南被尊为民族女英雄。

label.en: Raises revolt and is proclaimed queen
Takes Luy Lâu, seat of Jiaozhi
Defeated by Ma Yuan near Lãng Bạc
label.zh: 在浪泊附近被马援击败

sources.title: Hou Hanshu (Book of the Later Han), "Biography of Ma Yuan" and "Treatise on the Southern Man"
Keith W. Taylor, The Birth of Vietnam (University of California Press, 1983)
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Wikipedia: Trưng Trắc

note: Her birth year is unknown (Wikidata's 14 CE is traditional); battle sites are approximate.

role.en: King, founder of the Ngô dynasty

summary.en: A commander from Đường Lâm who avenged his father-in-law Dương Đình Nghệ, defeated the Southern Han at Bạch Đằng in 938 and proclaimed himself king at Cổ Loa, marking the start of lasting Vietnamese independence.
summary.zh: 唐林人，为岳父杨廷艺复仇，938年在白藤江击败南汉，随后在古螺称王，标志着越南长期独立的开端。

label.en: Proclaims himself king at Cổ Loa

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ngô Quyền
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Keith W. Taylor, The Birth of Vietnam (University of California Press, 1983)
Wikipedia: Ngô Quyền

summary.en: Khmer king (r. 1113–c. 1150) who reunited the empire, waged wars against Đại Việt and Champa, re-established diplomatic ties with China, and built Angkor Wat.
summary.zh: 高棉国王（1113—约1150年在位），重新统一帝国，对大越与占婆用兵，恢复与中国的外交往来，并修建了吴哥窟。

label.zh: 在耶输陀罗补罗夺得王位

label.en: Campaigns against Đại Việt in Nghệ An

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Suryavarman II
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: Suryavarman II

note: Birth year unknown (Wikidata gives 1094); the death date of c. 1150 is inferred from inscriptions.

summary.en: King of Pagan (r. 1044–1077) who united the Irrawaddy valley for the first time, conquered the Mon city of Thaton and championed Theravada Buddhism, laying the foundations of Burmese civilisation.
summary.zh: 蒲甘国王（1044—1077年在位），首次统一伊洛瓦底江流域，征服孟族城市直通，大力弘扬上座部佛教，奠定了缅甸文明的基础。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Anawrahta
Michael Aung-Thwin, Pagan: The Origins of Modern Burma (University of Hawaii Press, 1985)
Hmannan Yazawin (Glass Palace Chronicle, 1832)
Wikipedia: Anawrahta

note: Reign dates follow modern reconstructions; the chronicles differ.

summary.en: After expelling the Cham who had sacked Angkor in 1177, he was crowned in 1181 and became the greatest builder of the Khmer Empire: Angkor Thom, the Bayon, Ta Prohm, roads, rest houses and 102 hospitals. A devout Mahayana Buddhist, he also conquered Champa.
summary.zh: 1177年占婆攻陷吴哥后，他驱逐占婆军队，1181年加冕，成为高棉帝国最伟大的营建者：修建吴哥城、巴戎寺、塔布茏寺以及道路、驿站和一百零二所医院。他笃信大乘佛教，并征服了占婆。

label.en: Dedicates Ta Prohm to his mother
Builds Angkor Thom and the Bayon

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Jayavarman VII
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: Jayavarman VII

note: Birth and death years are approximate (c. 1122–c. 1218).

summary.en: Prince Trần Quốc Tuấn, supreme commander against the second and third Mongol invasions. His "Proclamation to the Officers" and his victory at Bạch Đằng in 1288 made him Vietnam's most revered military hero.
summary.zh: 陈国峻，陈朝宗室，抗击元朝第二、第三次入侵的最高统帅。其《檄将士文》及1288年白藤江大捷使他成为越南最受尊崇的军事英雄。

label.en: Fights in the first Mongol invasion
label.zh: 参与抗击第一次元军入侵

label.en: Issues the Proclamation to the Officers at Vạn Kiếp
Retakes Thăng Long from the Yuan

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Trần Hưng Đạo

Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Trần Hưng Đạo

summary.en: The chief minister of Majapahit who, according to the Pararaton, swore the Palapa oath to abstain from pleasures until he had united the archipelago. Under him and Hayam Wuruk, Majapahit claimed overlordship over much of maritime Southeast Asia.
summary.zh: 满者伯夷宰相。据《列王志》记载，他立下“帕拉帕誓言”，誓在统一群岛之前不享安逸。在他与哈亚·乌鲁克治下，满者伯夷宣称对东南亚海岛大部拥有宗主权。

label.en: Saves King Jayanegara during the Kuti revolt
label.zh: 在库提叛乱中救护国王查耶纳加拉

label.en: Swears the Palapa oath as mahapatih
label.zh: 出任宰相并立帕拉帕誓言

label.en: Bubat incident with the Sundanese royal party
label.zh: 与巽他王室发生布巴特事件

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Gajah Mada
Pararaton (Book of Kings, 15th–16th c.)
Mpu Prapañca, Deśawarṇana (Nāgarakṛtāgama, 1365), trans. Stuart Robson (KITLV, 1995)

Wikipedia: Gajah Mada

note: Known mainly from the Pararaton and Nāgarakṛtāgama; birth year and several episodes are uncertain or legendary.

summary.en: A prince of Palembang who fled Majapahit pressure to Temasek (Singapore) and, driven out again, founded Malacca around 1400. He secured Ming protection, visiting the Yongle Emperor in 1411.
summary.zh: 巨港王子，为躲避满者伯夷的压力逃往淡马锡（今新加坡），再度被逐后约于1400年建立马六甲。他寻求明朝庇护，并于1411年朝见永乐皇帝。

label.en: Visits the Ming court at Nanjing

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Parameswara
Sejarah Melayu (Malay Annals), trans. C. C. Brown (1952)
Tomé Pires, Suma Oriental (1512–1515), trans. Armando Cortesão (Hakluyt Society, 1944)
Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Wikipedia: Parameswara of Malacca

note: Malay, Portuguese and Chinese sources disagree on dates and on whether he converted to Islam.

summary.en: A datu of Mactan who refused to submit to Rajah Humabon of Cebu and his Spanish allies. His warriors killed Ferdinand Magellan in 1521, and he is honoured as the first Filipino hero to resist European colonisation.
summary.zh: 麦克坦的首领，拒绝臣服于宿务的胡马邦王及其西班牙盟友。1521年他的战士杀死了麦哲伦，被尊为第一位抵抗欧洲殖民的菲律宾英雄。

label.en: Refuses tribute; Spaniards burn a Mactan village
label.zh: 拒绝纳贡，西班牙人焚烧麦克坦村落

label.en: Defeats and kills Magellan at Mactan
label.zh: 在麦克坦击败并杀死麦哲伦

sources.title: Antonio Pigafetta, Relazione del primo viaggio intorno al mondo (c. 1524), trans. R. A. Skelton (1969)
Teodoro A. Agoncillo, The Revolt of the Masses: The Story of Bonifacio and the Katipunan (1956)
Wikipedia: Lapulapu

note: Pigafetta's account is the only contemporary source; birth and death years are traditional estimates.

summary.en: King of Toungoo Burma (r. 1550–1581) who built the largest empire in Southeast Asian history, conquering the Shan states, Lan Na, Manipur, Lan Xang and Ayutthaya, ruled from his capital at Pegu.
summary.zh: 东吁王朝国王（1550—1581年在位），征服掸邦、兰纳、曼尼普尔、澜沧与阿瑜陀耶，以勃固为都，建立了东南亚历史上疆域最大的帝国。

label.en: Second siege; Ayutthaya becomes a vassal
label.zh: 再次围攻，阿瑜陀耶臣服

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Bayinnaung
Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, Vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
Hmannan Yazawin (Glass Palace Chronicle, 1832)
G. E. Harvey, History of Burma (Longmans, 1925)
Wikipedia: Bayinnaung

role.en: Founder of the Later Lê dynasty

summary.en: A landowner of Lam Sơn who led the ten-year uprising that ended Ming occupation in 1427. Enthroned as Lê Thái Tổ in 1428, he is linked by legend to the returned sword of Hoàn Kiếm Lake.
summary.zh: 蓝山地主，领导十年起义，于1427年结束明朝统治。1428年即位为黎太祖，还剑湖“还剑”的传说即与他相关。

label.en: Born at Lam Sơn, Thanh Hóa
Ming relief army destroyed at Chi Lăng

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Lê Lợi (Lê Thái Tổ)
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Lê Lợi

summary.en: A Filipino ophthalmologist, polyglot and novelist whose Noli Me Tángere and El filibusterismo exposed abuses of Spanish colonial rule. Exiled to Dapitan and executed for alleged sedition in 1896, he became the national hero of the Philippines.
summary.zh: 菲律宾眼科医生、通晓多种语言的小说家，所著《不许犯我》和《起义者》揭露西班牙殖民统治的弊端。他被流放达皮丹，1896年以煽动叛乱罪遭处决，成为菲律宾国父式的民族英雄。

label.zh: 毕业于马尼拉雅典耀学校

label.en: Publishes Noli Me Tángere in Berlin

label.zh: 在马尼拉巴贡巴扬遭处决

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: José Rizal
Austin Coates, Rizal: Philippine Nationalist and Martyr (Oxford University Press, 1968)
Teodoro A. Agoncillo, The Revolt of the Masses: The Story of Bonifacio and the Katipunan (1956)
Wikipedia: José Rizal

role.en: Revolutionary and President of North Vietnam
role.zh: 革命家、越南民主共和国主席

summary.en: Born Nguyễn Sinh Cung in Nghệ An, he spent three decades abroad as a sailor, activist and Comintern agent before returning in 1941 to lead the Việt Minh. He proclaimed Vietnamese independence in 1945 and led North Vietnam until his death.
summary.zh: 本名阮生恭，生于义安，在海外以海员、活动家和共产国际成员身份度过三十年，1941年回国领导越盟。1945年他宣布越南独立，并领导越南北方直至逝世。

label.en: Born in Nam Đàn, Nghệ An
Sails from Saigon as a ship's cook
label.zh: 以船上厨工身份自西贡出海

label.en: Petitions the Versailles conference from Paris
label.zh: 在巴黎向凡尔赛和会递交请愿书
在广州组织越南革命青年

label.en: Returns to Vietnam at Pác Bó; founds the Việt Minh

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Hồ Chí Minh
William J. Duiker, Ho Chi Minh: A Life (Hyperion, 2000)
Fredrik Logevall, Embers of War: The Fall of an Empire and the Making of America's Vietnam (Random House, 2012)
Wikipedia: Ho Chi Minh

role.en: Nationalist leader and first President of Indonesia
role.zh: 民族主义领袖、印度尼西亚首任总统

summary.en: An engineer who founded the Indonesian Nationalist Party in 1927 and spent years in Dutch internal exile. He proclaimed independence in 1945, hosted the Bandung Conference and ruled under "Guided Democracy" until sidelined by Suharto in 1966–67.
summary.zh: 工程师出身，1927年创建印度尼西亚民族党，曾长期遭荷兰当局流放。1945年宣布独立，主办万隆会议，推行“有领导的民主”，1966—1967年被苏哈托架空。

label.zh: 在万隆创建印度尼西亚民族党
被流放至弗洛勒斯岛恩德

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sukarno
J. D. Legge, Sukarno: A Political Biography (Allen Lane, 1972)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: Sukarno

summary.en: Daughter of a Javanese regent, Kartini was secluded at home from the age of 12 but corresponded in Dutch with European friends about colonial injustice, polygamy and women's education. She opened a small school for girls and died after childbirth at 25; her letters, published in 1911, made her a national heroine of Indonesia.
summary.zh: 卡蒂妮是爪哇一位县长之女，12岁起被闭居家中，却用荷兰文与欧洲友人通信，探讨殖民不公、一夫多妻和女性教育。她开办了一所小型女子学校，25岁时死于产后并发症；1911年出版的书信集使她成为印度尼西亚的民族英雄。

sources.title: Britannica: Raden Adjeng Kartini
Wikipedia: Kartini
Joost Coté (trans.), Kartini: The Complete Writings 1898–1904 (2014)

summary.en: A woman of Jiuzhen (Thanh Hóa) who in 248 led a rising against the Eastern Wu governors of Jiaozhi. Vietnamese tradition pictures her riding an elephant into battle in golden armour and refusing to be "a concubine"; she died, by tradition by her own hand, when the revolt was crushed.
summary.zh: 九真郡（今清化）女子，248年起兵反抗东吴在交趾的统治。越南传说她身披金甲、骑象出战，并宣称不愿“为人婢妾”；起义被镇压后，相传她自尽身亡。

label.en: Born in Jiuzhen (Yên Định, Thanh Hóa)
Raises revolt from the Nưa mountain base
Dies on Mount Tùng; temple at Hậu Lộc
label.zh: 殁于松山，后禄建庙祭祀

sources.title: Sanguozhi (Records of the Three Kingdoms), Wu shu: biography of Lu Yin
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Keith W. Taylor, The Birth of Vietnam (University of California Press, 1983)
Wikipedia: Lady Triệu

note: Chinese records mention the 248 rising but not her; the heroine and her life are known from later Vietnamese tradition.

summary.en: A local official of Jiaozhou who drove out the Liang governor in 541, proclaimed himself Emperor of the South in 544 and named his state Vạn Xuân. Defeated by the Liang general Chen Baxian, he retreated into the hills and died in 548.
summary.zh: 交州地方官员，541年驱逐梁朝刺史，544年自称“南越帝”，定国号“万春”。后被梁将陈霸先击败，退入山区，548年去世。

label.en: Leads revolt against the Liang governor
Proclaimed emperor of Vạn Xuân at Long Biên
Dies in the Khuất Lão cave refuge

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Chen shu (Book of Chen), annals of Emperor Wu (Chen Baxian)
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Wikipedia: Lý Nam Đế

note: Birth year is traditional; sites of the 545–548 campaigns are approximate.

summary.en: A Khmer prince who, according to an 11th-century inscription, returned from "Java" and spent decades subduing rival chiefs before having himself consecrated universal monarch on Mahendraparvata (Phnom Kulen) in 802. He ruled from Hariharalaya near the later site of Angkor.
summary.zh: 高棉王子。据11世纪碑铭记载，他从“爪哇”归来，经数十年征服各地首领，802年在摩醯因陀罗山（荔枝山）举行仪式，自立为“转轮王”。他以吴哥附近的诃里诃罗洲为都。

label.en: Returns from "Java" and settles at Indrapura
label.zh: 从“爪哇”归来，驻因陀罗补罗
移驻诃里诃罗洲（罗洛士）
在荔枝山受封为转轮王

sources.title: George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Jayavarman II
Sdok Kak Thom inscription (K. 235, 1052)
Wikipedia: Jayavarman II

note: Britannica gives c. 770–850; some recent scholars date his death to 835. "Java" may mean a Malay polity rather than the island.

summary.en: A general of Anawrahta who survived exile under two kings to take the throne of Pagan in 1084. He reconciled Burmans and Mon, used Mon in his inscriptions, sent missions to restore the Mahabodhi temple at Bodh Gaya and built the Ananda Temple.
summary.zh: 阿奴律陀麾下大将，历经两朝流放，1084年登上蒲甘王位。他致力于缅人与孟人的和解，碑铭使用孟文，曾遣使修缮菩提伽耶的大菩提寺，并兴建阿难陀寺。

label.en: Fights in Anawrahta's conquest of Thaton
Crowned king after crushing the Pegu revolt

sources.title: G. H. Luce, Old Burma–Early Pagán (J. J. Augustin, 1969–70)
Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kyanzittha
Wikipedia: Kyansittha

note: Birth year and the end of his reign (1112 or 1113) are uncertain.

role.en: General and statesman of Đại Việt

summary.en: A palace eunuch who became Đại Việt's greatest general. He captured the Cham king in 1069, struck pre-emptively into Song China in 1075–1076, and in 1077 held the Như Nguyệt river line against the Song counter-invasion; the poem "Nam quốc sơn hà" is linked to that defence.
summary.zh: 宫廷宦官出身，后成为大越最杰出的将领。1069年俘获占城国王，1075—1076年先发制人攻入宋境，1077年在如月江防线击退宋军反攻；名诗《南国山河》即与此役相关。

label.en: Captures the Cham king at Vijaya
label.zh: 在毗阇耶俘获占城国王

label.en: Invades Song China, taking Qinzhou and Lianzhou
label.zh: 攻入宋境，夺取钦州、廉州
围邕州四十二日后破城

label.en: Defends the Như Nguyệt river line

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Songshi (History of Song), "Biography of Jiaozhi"
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Wikipedia: Lý Thường Kiệt

summary.en: The third king of Sukhothai, who earned his name ("Rama the Bold") in single combat as a youth and extended his overlordship to the Malay Peninsula and Laos. Thai tradition credits him with the Thai alphabet and the famous inscription of 1292.
summary.zh: 素可泰第三代国王，少年时在单挑中获胜，得名“勇敢的拉玛”，其宗主权远及马来半岛和老挝。泰国传统认为他创制了泰文字母，并留下著名的1292年碑铭。

label.en: Defeats Khun Sam Chon of Mueang Chot on elephant-back
label.zh: 在象战中击败达城（孟乔）城主坤三春

sources.title: Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
A. B. Griswold & Prasert na Nagara, "The Inscription of King Rāma Gamhèn of Sukhodaya (1292 A.D.)", Journal of the Siam Society 59 (1971)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ramkhamhaeng
Wikipedia: Ram Khamhaeng

note: Birth year is approximate; the authenticity of the 1292 inscription has been challenged.

summary.en: Ruler of Ngoenyang on the upper Mekong who founded Chiang Rai in 1262, conquered the Mon kingdom of Haripunchai, and in 1296 founded Chiang Mai as capital of Lan Na. His law code, the Mangraisat, was used in the north for centuries.
summary.zh: 湄公河上游恩央国的统治者，1262年建清莱，后征服孟人哈里奔猜国，1296年建清迈为兰纳都城。他颁行的《孟莱法典》在泰北沿用数百年。

sources.title: David K. Wyatt & Aroonrut Wichienkeeo (trans.), The Chiang Mai Chronicle (Silkworm Books, 2nd ed. 1998)
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
Wikipedia: Mangrai

note: The chronicle says he was killed by lightning in a Chiang Mai market; the date of Haripunchai's fall is given as 1281 or 1292.

summary.en: An exiled prince of Muang Sua raised at Angkor, who returned with a Khmer army and in 1353 founded Lan Xang, "a million elephants". Lao tradition credits his Khmer queen with bringing Theravada Buddhism; his nobles deposed him in 1373.
summary.zh: 孟骚流亡王子，在吴哥长大，率高棉军队返回，1353年建立“百万大象”澜沧王国。老挝传统认为是他的高棉王后引入了上座部佛教；1373年他被贵族废黜。

label.en: Raised in exile at the Khmer court of Angkor
label.zh: 在吴哥的高棉宫廷流亡长大

label.en: Crowned at Xieng Dong Xieng Thong

sources.title: Martin Stuart-Fox, A History of Laos (Cambridge University Press, 1997)
Martin Stuart-Fox, The Lao Kingdom of Lān Xāng: Rise and Decline (White Lotus, 1998)
Wikipedia: Fa Ngum

note: Known mainly from later Lao chronicles; dates are traditional. He was deposed c. 1373; Britannica gives his death as 1374, while Lao tradition has him die in exile in Nan in 1393.

name.zh: 哈亚·乌鲁克（拉惹沙纳伽拉）

summary.en: Majapahit's king at its height, ruling with the chief minister Gajah Mada until 1364. The court poet Prapanca's Nagarakretagama describes his royal progresses through East Java and lists the far-flung lands said to pay tribute to him.
summary.zh: 满者伯夷鼎盛时期的国王，1364年前与宰相加查·马达共同执政。宫廷诗人普拉潘扎的《爪哇史颂》描写了他巡游东爪哇的盛况，并列出据称向其纳贡的遥远诸国。

label.en: Born at Trowulan, the Majapahit capital
label.zh: 生于满者伯夷都城特罗武兰

label.en: Bubat tragedy: his Sundanese bride dies
label.zh: 布巴特惨剧，巽他新娘殒命

summary.en: Lê Lợi's chief adviser in the war against Ming occupation, who wrote its manifesto of victory, the "Great Proclamation upon the Pacification of the Wu" (1428). A pioneer of poetry in Nôm script, he was executed with his family in 1442 after the sudden death of the young king Lê Thái Tông.
summary.zh: 黎利抗明战争的首席谋士，撰写了胜利宣言《平吴大诰》（1428年）。他是喃字诗歌的先驱；1442年年轻的黎太宗暴卒后，他被株连三族处死。

label.zh: 在南关送别被押往中国的父亲

summary.en: The Later Lê emperor who reorganised Đại Việt on Confucian lines, issued the Hồng Đức legal code and had the national annals compiled. In 1471 he destroyed the Cham capital Vijaya and pushed the frontier south to the Cù Mông pass.
summary.zh: 后黎朝皇帝，按儒家原则改组大越，颁布《洪德法典》，并命人编纂国史。1471年他攻破占城都城毗阇耶，将边界推进到瞿蒙关。

summary.en: A Siamese prince taken to Pegu as a hostage after Bayinnaung's conquest, who renounced Burmese overlordship in 1584 and repelled repeated invasions. Thai tradition celebrates his elephant duel at Nong Sarai in 1593; he died on campaign in the Shan hills in 1605.
summary.zh: 暹罗王子，莽应龙征服阿瑜陀耶后被押往勃固为人质。1584年他宣布脱离缅甸宗主权，多次击退缅军入侵。泰国传统颂扬他1593年在农沙莱的象战；1605年他死于掸邦山区的征途中。

label.en: Taken as a hostage to Pegu
Dies on campaign at Mueang Haeng

sources.title: Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Ayutthaya (Cambridge University Press, 2017)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Naresuan
Wikipedia: Naresuan

note: The location of his independence declaration (Kraeng) and of his death are approximate.

story.en:
Naresuan grew up as the son of a defeated king. When Bayinnaung took Phitsanulok in 1564, the boy was sent to Pegu as a hostage, and he spent his youth at the Burmese court, learning the warfare of the empire he would later fight. Returned in 1571 to govern Phitsanulok, he built up a personal army of loyal retainers.

In 1584, ordered to help Burma against a rebellion, he instead poured water from a golden vessel and declared that Ayutthaya was no longer Pegu's vassal. Four Burmese invasions followed. The most famous ended in January 1593 near Nong Sarai, where, according to Thai chronicles, Naresuan challenged the Burmese crown prince Mingyi Swa to combat on elephant-back and killed him with a blow of his glaive. Burmese chronicles tell it differently, but the invasion collapsed.

Naresuan went on the offensive, raiding as far as Pegu and Toungoo, and Ayutthaya regained a century of prosperity. He died in 1605 while marching against a Burmese-held Shan state. Thai films, coins and military academies still bear his image.
story.zh:
纳黎萱是战败国王之子。1564年莽应龙攻下彭世洛，他被送往勃固作人质，在缅甸宫廷度过少年时代，学会了这个他日后要与之作战的帝国的兵法。1571年他被遣回出任彭世洛城主，并组建了一支效忠于他的私人军队。

1584年，缅甸命他协助平叛，他却以金瓶洒水为誓，宣布阿瑜陀耶不再是勃固的藩属。此后缅军四次入侵。最著名的一次在1593年1月于农沙莱附近结束：据泰国编年史记载，纳黎萱向缅甸王储明吉斯瓦提出象背决斗，并用长柄战刀将其斩杀。缅甸史书的说法不同，但这次入侵确实就此瓦解。

纳黎萱随即转守为攻，兵锋远至勃固和东吁，阿瑜陀耶重获一个世纪的繁荣。1605年他在进攻缅甸控制的掸邦途中去世。至今泰国的电影、钱币和军校仍以他的形象为标志。

summary.en: Aceh's most powerful sultan, who conquered the pepper ports of Sumatra and the Malay peninsula, ruled with a mix of Islamic law and royal terror, and lost his great fleet in the failed attack on Portuguese Malacca in 1629.
summary.zh: 亚齐最强大的苏丹，征服了苏门答腊和马来半岛的胡椒港口，以伊斯兰法与王权威慑并用进行统治。1629年进攻葡属马六甲失败，损失了整支大舰队。

label.en: His armada is destroyed before Malacca
label.zh: 舰队在马六甲城下覆没

summary.en: The ruthless architect of Dutch power in Asia, who seized Jayakarta and founded Batavia in 1619 and conquered the Banda Islands in 1621 with the killing and deportation of most of their people. He died in Batavia during Sultan Agung's second siege.
summary.zh: 荷兰在亚洲势力的冷酷缔造者。1619年他夺取雅加特拉并建立巴达维亚，1621年征服班达群岛，岛上居民大多遭屠杀或流放。他在苏丹阿贡第二次围攻巴达维亚期间死于城中。

summary.en: The greatest ruler of Islamic Mataram, who subdued Surabaya and most of Java, twice besieged Dutch Batavia (1628, 1629) and fused the Islamic lunar calendar with the Javanese Saka year. He built the royal cemetery at Imogiri, where he is buried.
summary.zh: 伊斯兰马打兰最伟大的君主，征服泗水和爪哇大部，两次围攻荷兰人的巴达维亚（1628、1629年），并把伊斯兰阴历与爪哇塞迦纪年融为一体。他修建了伊莫吉里王陵，死后葬于此。

summary.en: A village headman of Moksobo who rallied resistance after a restored Mon kingdom captured Ava in 1752. In eight years he reunified Burma, founded Rangoon, destroyed Pegu and invaded Siam; he died of illness on the retreat from Ayutthaya.
summary.zh: 木疏于村头人。1752年复兴的孟人王国攻陷阿瓦后，他组织抵抗，八年内重新统一缅甸，建立仰光，摧毁勃固并入侵暹罗；在从阿瑜陀耶撤军途中病逝。

summary.en: Son of a Teochew Chinese father and a Thai mother, governor of Tak, who broke out of besieged Ayutthaya in 1767, rebuilt an army on the east coast and within months drove the Burmese out. He reunited Siam from Thonburi, but grew erratic and was deposed and executed in 1782.
summary.zh: 父亲为潮州人，母亲为泰人，曾任达府府尹。1767年他从被围的阿瑜陀耶突围，在东海岸重建军队，数月内驱逐缅军，并以吞武里为都重新统一暹罗。晚年行为失常，1782年被废黜处死。

summary.en: The military genius of the Tây Sơn brothers, who crushed a Siamese invasion at Rạch Gầm–Xoài Mút in 1785, overthrew the Trịnh in 1786, and in 1789 routed a Qing army at Thăng Long in a lightning Tết offensive. He died suddenly at 39.

summary.en: The only Nguyễn prince to escape the Tây Sơn massacre of 1777, he fought for 25 years from bases in the Mekong delta, with Siamese support and French volunteers recruited by Bishop Pigneau de Behaine. In 1802 he united Vietnam and ruled from Huế.
summary.zh: 1777年西山军屠戮阮主家族时唯一逃脱的阮氏王子。他以湄公河三角洲为基地征战25年，得到暹罗支持和百多禄主教招募的法国志愿者相助，1802年统一越南，定都顺化。

summary.en: Vietnam's national poet. A Lê loyalist who reluctantly served the Nguyễn, he retold a Chinese novel as the Truyện Kiều, 3,254 lines of six-eight verse in Nôm script about a woman who sells herself to save her family, a work still quoted daily in Vietnam.

summary.en: An East India Company clerk who rose to govern Java during the British interregnum of 1811–1816, wrote a History of Java, and in 1819 founded a free port at Singapore. He also founded the Zoological Society of London.
summary.zh: 东印度公司书记员出身，1811—1816年英国暂据期间出任爪哇副总督，著有《爪哇史》，1819年在新加坡建立自由港。他还创建了伦敦动物学会。

label.zh: 生于牙买加外海的船上

label.zh: 建立新加坡英国殖民地

Victoria Glendinning, Raffles and the Golden Opportunity (Profile, 2012)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sir Stamford Raffles
Wikipedia: Stamford Raffles

role.en: Javanese prince, leader of the Java War
role.zh: 爪哇亲王，爪哇战争领袖

summary.en: Eldest son of the Sultan of Yogyakarta, a mystic who believed himself destined to be the Ratu Adil, the "just king". When the Dutch drove a road across his estate at Tegalrejo in 1825 he rose in a five-year war; lured to negotiations at Magelang in 1830, he was arrested and exiled.
summary.zh: 日惹苏丹的长子，一位神秘主义者，自信是天命所归的“正义之王”。1825年荷兰人在他的德加勒佐庄园修路，他由此发动长达五年的战争；1830年被诱至马格朗谈判时遭逮捕并流放。

sources.title: Peter Carey, The Power of Prophecy: Prince Dipanagara and the End of an Old Order in Java, 1785–1855 (KITLV, 2007)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Wikipedia: Diponegoro

story.en:
Diponegoro was born in 1785 into the court of Yogyakarta, the eldest son of the future sultan Hamengkubuwono III, but by a lesser wife. Raised by his great-grandmother at the country estate of Tegalrejo, he grew up among village religious teachers and spent long periods meditating in caves and at the shrines of Java's old kings, where he had visions that he would become the Ratu Adil, the just king of Javanese prophecy.

By the 1820s Yogyakarta was in crisis: the Dutch were taking over court lands, tollgates squeezed the peasants, and a cholera epidemic and crop failure added to the misery. When the Dutch drove a road across his estate in July 1825, marking it with stakes, his followers pulled them up and he raised the banner of holy war. For five years his forces fought a guerrilla war across central Java; the Dutch answered with a chain of fortified posts, the benteng stelsel. Some 200,000 Javanese died, most from famine and disease.

In March 1830 the Dutch general De Kock invited him to talks at Magelang during Ramadan and arrested him. Exiled to Manado and then Makassar, he wrote his autobiography, the Babad Diponegoro, now on UNESCO's Memory of the World register.
story.zh:
蒂博尼哥罗1785年生于日惹宫廷，是后来的苏丹哈孟古布沃诺三世的长子，但生母地位较低。他由曾祖母在乡间庄园德加勒佐抚养长大，与乡村宗教教师为伍，并常在山洞和爪哇古代君王的圣陵中长时间冥想，在幻象中得知自己将成为爪哇预言中的“正义之王”。

到19世纪20年代，日惹陷入危机：荷兰人侵占宫廷土地，关卡税压榨农民，霍乱流行和歉收更使民不聊生。1825年7月，荷兰人修路穿过他的庄园并打桩标界，他的追随者拔掉木桩，他随即举起圣战大旗。五年间，他的军队在中爪哇各地开展游击战；荷兰人则以一连串设防哨所（堡垒体系）应对。约二十万爪哇人死亡，大多死于饥荒和疾病。

1830年3月，正值斋月，荷兰将军德科克邀他到马格朗谈判，随即将他逮捕。他被流放到万鸦老，后又移囚望加锡，在那里写下自传《蒂博尼哥罗纪事》，该书现已列入联合国教科文组织《世界记忆名录》。

role.en: Guerrilla leader of the Aceh War

summary.en: An Acehnese noblewoman who fought the Dutch for a quarter-century after her first husband fell in 1878. With her second husband Teuku Umar, and after his death in 1899 alone, she led guerrillas in the western highlands until, nearly blind, she was captured in 1905 and exiled to Sumedang in Java.
summary.zh: 亚齐贵族女子，1878年第一任丈夫阵亡后与荷兰人周旋了四分之一个世纪。她与第二任丈夫特乌库·乌马尔并肩作战，1899年乌马尔死后独自率领西部山区的游击队，直到1905年近乎失明时被俘，流放爪哇的苏美当。

label.en: First husband killed; vows to fight on
label.zh: 首任丈夫阵亡，誓言继续战斗
特乌库·乌马尔在默拉务附近阵亡

Susan Blackburn, Women and the State in Modern Indonesia (Cambridge University Press, 2004)
Wikipedia: Cut Nyak Dhien

summary.en: The modernising king who abolished slavery and prostration at court, built a centralised bureaucracy, railways and schools, and kept Siam independent by ceding Laos and western Cambodia to France and the northern Malay states to Britain. He toured Europe in 1897 and 1907.
summary.zh: 推行现代化的国王，废除奴隶制和宫廷跪拜礼，建立中央集权的官僚体系、铁路和学校。他以向法国割让老挝和柬埔寨西部、向英国割让北部马来诸邦为代价，保住了暹罗的独立。1897年和1907年两度出访欧洲。

label.en: Born in the Grand Palace, Bangkok

label.zh: 出访新加坡与巴达维亚

label.en: Tours Europe; received by Queen Victoria
label.zh: 出访欧洲，受维多利亚女王接见

David K. Wyatt, The Politics of Reform in Thailand (Yale University Press, 1969)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Chulalongkorn
Wikipedia: Chulalongkorn

summary.en: A self-taught Manila warehouse clerk who founded the secret society Katipunan in 1892 and launched the revolution against Spain in August 1896. Outmanoeuvred by Emilio Aguinaldo's faction at the Tejeros convention, he was tried for sedition and executed by fellow revolutionaries.
summary.zh: 自学成才的马尼拉仓库职员，1892年创立秘密团体卡蒂普南，1896年8月发动反西班牙革命。在特赫罗斯会议上被阿奎纳多一派压倒，后以叛乱罪受审，被革命同志处决。

label.zh: 在马尼拉创立卡蒂普南

label.en: "Cry of Pugad Lawin" begins the revolution
label.zh: “普加德拉温呐喊”揭开革命序幕
在特赫罗斯会议上失势

sources.title: Teodoro A. Agoncillo, The Revolt of the Masses: The Story of Bonifacio and the Katipunan (University of the Philippines, 1956)
Teodoro A. Agoncillo, History of the Filipino People (8th ed., Garotech, 1990)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Andrés Bonifacio
Wikipedia: Andrés Bonifacio

story.en:
Andrés Bonifacio was orphaned at fourteen and supported his siblings by making canes and paper fans, then by clerking for foreign trading firms. He read voraciously: José Rizal's novels, histories of the French Revolution, Victor Hugo. When Rizal was deported in July 1892, Bonifacio and a few friends founded the Kataastaasan, Kagalanggalangang Katipunan ng mga Anak ng Bayan, a secret brotherhood sworn in blood to win independence by arms.

By 1896 it had tens of thousands of members. When the Spanish discovered it in August, Bonifacio gathered his followers in the hills north of Manila, where, according to the participants' later accounts, they tore up their cedulas, the tax certificates that marked colonial subjection, and launched the uprising.

The revolution's successes, however, came in Cavite, under local leaders led by Emilio Aguinaldo. At the Tejeros convention of March 1897 Aguinaldo was elected president and Bonifacio's credentials were insulted. He refused to accept the result, was arrested, tried for treason and shot on 10 May 1897. Filipinos now honour him on 30 November as the "Father of the Revolution".
story.zh:
安德烈斯·博尼法西奥十四岁成为孤儿，靠制作手杖和纸扇、后来又在外国商行当职员养活弟妹。他如饥似渴地阅读黎刹的小说、法国大革命史和雨果的作品。1892年7月黎刹被流放后，博尼法西奥与几位朋友创立了“国民之子最崇高最可敬协会”（卡蒂普南），成员歃血为盟，誓以武力争取独立。

到1896年，协会已有数万名成员。同年8月组织被西班牙人发现，博尼法西奥在马尼拉以北的山间召集追随者。据参与者事后回忆，他们撕毁了象征殖民臣属地位的纳税证，宣告起义。

然而革命的胜利却出现在甲米地，由阿奎纳多为首的当地领袖取得。1897年3月的特赫罗斯会议上，阿奎纳多当选总统，博尼法西奥的资历则受到羞辱。他拒不接受结果，遭逮捕并以叛国罪受审，1897年5月10日被枪决。如今菲律宾人在每年11月30日纪念这位“革命之父”。

role.en: Revolutionary leader, first president of the Philippines
role.zh: 革命领袖，菲律宾第一任总统

summary.en: Mayor of Kawit who became the revolution's military leader in Cavite, declared independence from Spain on 12 June 1898 and headed the Malolos Republic. He led resistance to the United States until his capture at Palanan in 1901, and lived to see independence in 1946.
summary.zh: 甲米地卡维特镇镇长，后成为革命的军事领袖。1898年6月12日宣布脱离西班牙独立，出任马洛洛斯共和国总统，领导抗美战争直至1901年在帕拉南被俘。他活到亲眼看到1946年菲律宾独立。

summary.en: A student radical who trained the "Thirty Comrades" with Japan, led the Burma Independence Army into Burma in 1942, turned against the Japanese in 1945 and negotiated independence with Attlee in 1947. He was assassinated with six ministers months before independence.

story.en:
In 1940 Aung San, the 25-year-old secretary of the nationalist Thakin movement, slipped out of Burma with a warrant on his head, hoping to find Chinese communists. Japanese agents found him first. He and twenty-nine other young Burmese, the "Thirty Comrades", were trained in secret on Hainan island, and in 1942 marched into Burma behind the Japanese army as the Burma Independence Army.

The independence Japan granted in 1943 proved hollow. On 27 March 1945, now commander of the Burma National Army, Aung San led his troops out of Rangoon in an apparent parade and turned them against the Japanese, a date still marked as Armed Forces Day.

After the war he outplayed the British: in January 1947 he signed an agreement with Clement Attlee in London promising independence within a year, and at Panglong in February he won the Shan, Kachin and Chin leaders to a federal union. On 19 July 1947, gunmen sent by his rival U Saw burst into a cabinet meeting and killed him and six colleagues. Burma became independent without him, and his daughter Aung San Suu Kyi later led the struggle against its military rulers.
story.zh:
1940年，25岁的德钦党总书记昂山在通缉令下秘密离开缅甸，本想寻找中国共产党，却先被日本特工找到。他和另外29名缅甸青年（即“三十志士”）在海南岛秘密受训，1942年作为“缅甸独立军”随日军打回缅甸。

1943年日本给予的“独立”有名无实。1945年3月27日，已任缅甸国民军司令的昂山率部以阅兵为名开出仰光，随即掉转枪口攻击日军，这一天至今仍是缅甸的建军节。

战后他在谈判中占得上风：1947年1月在伦敦与艾德礼签署协定，英国承诺一年内给予独立；2月又在彬龙说服掸、克钦、钦族领袖加入联邦。1947年7月19日，政敌吴素派出的枪手闯入内阁会议，杀死了昂山和六名同僚。缅甸在他身后获得独立，他的女儿昂山素季后来领导了反对军政府的斗争。

role.en: General of the Vietnamese People's Army

summary.en: A history teacher turned self-taught general, who founded the Viet Minh's first armed unit in 1944, defeated the French at Điện Biên Phủ in 1954 and remained defence minister through the war against the United States and South Vietnam, though Lê Duẩn and other party leaders increasingly set strategy. He died aged 102.
summary.zh: 由历史教师自学成才的将军。1944年组建越盟第一支武装部队，1954年在奠边府击败法军，在对美国和南越的战争中一直担任国防部长，但战略日益由黎笋等党的领导人主导。享年102岁。

summary.en: A prince of Kedah who led UMNO and the cross-communal Alliance to independence, proclaimed Merdeka in 1957, created Malaysia in 1963 and separated Singapore from it in 1965. He resigned after the communal riots of May 1969.

summary.en: A Cambridge-trained lawyer who co-founded the People's Action Party, became prime minister of self-governing Singapore in 1959, and after the 1965 separation from Malaysia built a disciplined, export-led city-state. He governed until 1990.
summary.zh: 剑桥大学毕业的律师，人民行动党创始人之一，1959年出任自治邦新加坡总理。1965年脱离马来西亚后，他把新加坡建设成纪律严明、以出口为导向的城市国家，执政至1990年。

summary.en: Born Saloth Sar to a prosperous farming family, he became a communist as a student in Paris, led the Communist Party of Kampuchea from 1963 and ruled Democratic Kampuchea from 1975 to 1979, when perhaps a quarter of Cambodians died. He died in the jungle at Anlong Veng, never tried.
